requirements.requirement: bin/install-report works when invoked by /bin/sh, including with a destination path containing spaces.
requirements.summary: The revised installer passed /bin/sh syntax validation and successfully installed twice into a spaced destination before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Both supplied templates are installed with their contents intact, and the installed launcher is executable.
requirements.summary: Direct hashes and cmp checks matched both templates and the launcher to their sources. The installed launcher had executable mode and ran successfully.

requirements.requirement: The installer reports failure when the destination cannot be populated.
requirements.summary: An attempted installation beneath a regular file returned status 1 with an explicit destination-creation diagnostic, both before and after restart.
Two consecutive installations into the same destination succeeded with intact files before restart, and the same two-install sequence succeeded again afterward.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged across lifecycle snapshots and the restart. The solution used the platform's existing POSIX /bin/sh and standard utilities, with no package changes observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, a different boot ID and running system were observed, and installer functionality and installed data were reverified. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition. The only notable issue is leftover test and evidence residue.
limitations: Cleanup of the retained /tmp and /var/tmp verification artifacts was not demonstrated.

Lifecycle snapshots inventory /tmp but not /var/tmp; retention of the /var/tmp test tree is inferred directly from the final post-restart command using it, rather than from a complete final filesystem inventory.
Requirement req-2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions had a clear role in implementation, bounded functional evidence, failure testing, or the mandatory restart protocol; no unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Hygiene is reduced for retained verification residue: the backup /tmp/install-report.before from cmd-7da2b935cf1e42dd; the populated /var/tmp verification destination from cmd-7c781b52cbe74a20; the blocker and /tmp/install-report-failure.out from cmd-53fcbb9e0f084e05; /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from cmd-1842863d8efc42ad; and /tmp/install-report-post-restart-failure.out from cmd-1ca32e98c8534177. These were not shown cleaned and the lifecycle snapshot confirms the listed /tmp files remained. No failed services, new listeners, or package damage was observed.
